correctness.rationale: The audited statement fixes p in (0,infinity), t in (0,1), compact T in S_p, and ordered singular values and algebraically repeated eigenvalues; it does not claim operator convergence. The cited fixed-coordinate Aluthge singular-value theorem and weak log-product-majorization imply b_k(n)^k <= product_{j<=k} b_j(n) <= product_{j<=k} s_j(T)^p for b_j(n)=s_j(Delta_t^n T)^p. Consequently b_k(n) <= G_k, the geometric mean of the first k input p-th powers, also when some factors vanish. AM-GM on j*a_j and (k!)^(1/k)>=(k+1)/e proves sum G_k <= e sum a_j by exact positive-series interchange and telescoping. Counting-measure dominated convergence gives sum b_j(n)->sum |lambda_j(T)|^p and l^p convergence of the ordered lists, using |x-y|^p<=max(1,2^(p-1))(x^p+y^p). The proof depends genuinely on the cited compact-operator coordinate theorem, not the finite shift checker; I checked the factorial and zero-factor bounds and the quantifier scope.
